slowest_experiments.experiment: V632 exact Markdown and YAML task-contract preflight

summary: Two experiments completed in 0.3 minutes, and one was compute-bound. The synthesis-only preflight took 0.28 minutes. Qwen3.8 claim/evidence structured trace capture was the sole and therefore longest compute-bound experiment at 0.01 minutes; no data available this milestone explains its duration, and no verified compute-bound GPU-idle condition is recorded.
bottlenecks_identified: V632 exact Markdown and YAML task-contract preflight was the longest entry at 0.28 minutes, but the data contains no causal breakdown; its synthesis-only status means GPU inactivity is expected.
Disk-mtime reconstruction provides task durations but no phase timing, so the cause of the 0.01-minute compute duration cannot be identified.
No task-scoped GPU samples, model-count receipt, or runner-selection record is available, so no data available this milestone establishes a two-or-more-model task or a missed DualGPURunner launch.
improvements_suggested: Cache exact Markdown and YAML contract-preflight results by input and validator version.
Emit monotonic task and phase timestamps instead of relying only on disk modification times.
Capture GPU samples inside each compute-task window and attach task and process ownership.
Record loaded-model count and runner selection in every compute launch receipt.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add content-addressed caching to the Markdown and YAML contract preflight.
Add one task-scoped envelope for phase timing and compute-window GPU samples.
Persist model-count and runner-selection evidence for every compute launch.
meta_reflection: The timing ranking identifies contract preflight as the only plausible optimization target, but the data does not establish why it took longer. A measured savings claim needs a cached-versus-uncached comparison and task-scoped compute telemetry.
